description: The Snowflake Scripting error variables SQLCODE, SQLERRM and SQLSTATE, available inside an EXCEPTION handler. A user-defined exception exposes its DECLARED code and message with SQLSTATE 'P0001'; division by zero maps to its Snowflake code 100051 and state '22012'; a missing object reports SQLSTATE '42S02' and an SQLERRM naming the failing object. SQLCODE carries no declared type, so RETURNing it directly makes the result TEXT - which is why the code assertions here are strings. The variables are usable in DML inside the handler through the BIND form, :SQLCODE and :SQLERRM: written bare inside an INSERT they would be column names. And their values are HANDLER-SCOPED, so a nested handled block restores the enclosing handler's values rather than leaving the inner exception's behind. Converted 1:1 from scripting/SqlErrorVariablesTest (now retired).

steps.sql: DECLARE e EXCEPTION (-20001, 'boom'); BEGIN RAISE e; EXCEPTION WHEN e THEN RETURN SQLCODE; END
DECLARE e EXCEPTION (-20001, 'boom'); BEGIN RAISE e; EXCEPTION WHEN e THEN RETURN SQLERRM; END
DECLARE e EXCEPTION (-20001, 'boom'); BEGIN RAISE e; EXCEPTION WHEN e THEN RETURN SQLSTATE; END
BEGIN RETURN 1 / 0; EXCEPTION WHEN OTHER THEN RETURN SQLSTATE; END
BEGIN RETURN 1 / 0; EXCEPTION WHEN OTHER THEN RETURN SQLCODE; END
BEGIN RETURN 1 / 0; EXCEPTION WHEN OTHER THEN RETURN SQLERRM; END
BEGIN SELECT * FROM no_such_table_xyz; EXCEPTION WHEN OTHER THEN RETURN SQLSTATE; END
BEGIN SELECT * FROM no_such_table_xyz; EXCEPTION WHEN OTHER THEN RETURN REPLACE(UPPER(SPLIT_PART(SQLERRM, ' Your primary role', 1)), CHAR(10), ' '); END

expect.value: SQL COMPILATION ERROR: OBJECT 'NO_SUCH_TABLE_XYZ' DOES NOT EXIST OR NOT AUTHORIZED.

steps.sql: CREATE TABLE err_log (code INTEGER, msg VARCHAR)
DECLARE e EXCEPTION (-20007, 'kaput'); BEGIN RAISE e; EXCEPTION WHEN e THEN INSERT INTO err_log VALUES (:SQLCODE, :SQLERRM); RETURN 'ok'; END
DECLARE e1 EXCEPTION (-20001, 'outer'); e2 EXCEPTION (-20002, 'inner'); BEGIN RAISE e1; EXCEPTION WHEN e1 THEN BEGIN RAISE e2; EXCEPTION WHEN e2 THEN NULL; END; RETURN SQLCODE || ':' || SQLERRM; END
